setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. No channel is muted, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press channel button (1,1) and let go after about half a second, well before one second is up. A short press only selects the channel, so the button stays bright and nothing is muted.
steps.title: Select channel 1 without muting

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: channel 1 plays C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65), and the strip below lists the four notes. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear channel one

steps.caption: Hold (1,1) for a full second, then let go. The button dims to show channel 1 is muted; a muted channel still counts as selected.
steps.title: Mute with a long press

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen for about a second and a half: the dimmed channel sends no notes, and the strip below stays empty. Playback keeps running, so the other channels would carry on.
steps.title: Listen to the muted channel

steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens again, so channel 1 is unmuted.
steps.title: Unmute with K1

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8): with channel 1 unmuted, C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65) sound again. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Hear it again

steps.caption: Tap Play. While the phrase sounds, hold (1,1) for a full second: the button dims and the notes stop. The clock keeps running, but no new notes sound for the next second and a half.
steps.title: Mute while it plays

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens and the phrase comes back in time with the running pattern, picking up wherever the loop has reached rather than starting over.
steps.title: Bring channel one back

title: Mute a channel and bring a running phrase back
